definition: Short stable study label, first author and year plus a letter if needed (e.g. Smith2021a). Same value on every row of the study. Use the same label in the RoB 2 and GRADE files.
Outcome key from the protocol outcome list (lower_snake_case, e.g. whole_blood_nad, sbp, fasting_glucose). One key per construct and matrix; different assay matrices are different outcomes.

Timepoint label for this result (e.g. wk6, wk12, day 21). Every arm of one comparison must use the same label. Put a number and unit in the label; a label with no number (e.g. 'end') cannot be ordered, so fill timepoint_weeks for it. The protocol says which timepoint enters the primary analysis when a study reports several.
parallel or crossover. Same value on every row of the study.
Arm label as reported (e.g. NR 1000 mg/day, placebo). For a crossover trial the arm is the treatment condition (NR period or control period), not the sequence.
1 for the comparator arm (placebo or no treatment), 0 for an NR arm. Exactly one control row per study x outcome x timepoint.

Participants analysed for this outcome in this arm at this timepoint (not the number randomised, unless they are the same). Crossover: participants contributing data to the paired analysis; same n on both rows.
Arm mean at the timepoint (final value, post-intervention).

SD of the final value. Leave blank if only an SE or CI is reported; do not hand-convert SE to SD here. Many NR papers report mean +/- SEM: check the table footnote and enter an SEM in se, never in sd. An SD of 0 is accepted only if another arm of the comparison has an SD above 0 (the comparison variance must be > 0); check that it was not rounded to 0.

SE of the arm mean when no SD is reported. If only a 95% CI for the arm mean is reported, enter se = (upper - lower) / (2 * t(0.975, n-1)) and record the original CI in notes (Cochrane Handbook 6.5.2.2).
Arm median at the timepoint, when the mean is not reported.
First quartile (25th percentile) at the timepoint.
Third quartile (75th percentile) at the timepoint.
Minimum at the timepoint.
Maximum at the timepoint.
Mean change from baseline (timepoint minus baseline), as reported. Sign convention: later minus earlier.
SD of the change from baseline, as reported. If only the SE of the change is reported, leave this blank and fill se_change.
Arm mean at baseline. Needed to impute an SD of change or to estimate corr_prepost from a study that reports all three SDs.
Arm SD at baseline.
Baseline to follow-up correlation, only if the study reports it or it can be computed from baseline, final and change SDs. Blank means the config default (0.5) is used.

Crossover only: within-person correlation between the NR-period and control-period measurements, if reported or derivable. Blank means the config default (0.5) is used. Leave blank for parallel trials.

Reported NR-minus-control mean difference, entered on the NR row (is_control = 0), blank on the control row. Crossover: the within-person difference from a paired or period-adjusted analysis (preferred to period means). Parallel: a reported between-group MD (e.g. ANCOVA-adjusted), used as it stands for MD analyses only (generic inverse variance); then the control row may be omitted. At most one such parallel comparison per study: several MDs against one shared control cannot be entered (Handbook 23.3.4).
SE of paired_md, on the same row. From a 95% CI in a small trial use (upper - lower) / (2 t(0.975, df)) with the trial's df, not 3.92 (Handbook 6.5.2.3).
NR dose in mg per day for this arm (0 for the control arm), as reported by the trial. Most trials report NR chloride; record the salt form in notes.
Time from start of supplementation to this timepoint, in weeks (days / 7). Crossover: length of each treatment period.
Population category from the protocol list (e.g. healthy_older, obesity_insulin_resistance, disease_<name>). Same value on every row of the study.
Overall RoB 2 judgement for this study result (this outcome and timepoint), copied from rob2_summary_template.csv after consensus.
Source of each number (table, figure, page, digitised, author contact), unit conversions applied, CI or P values converted, and anything a second extractor needs to reproduce the row.
SE of the change from baseline when no SD of change is reported. The engines convert it (SD = SE x sqrt(n), Handbook 6.5.2.2); do not hand-convert.
The timepoint in weeks, used by the engines to order timepoints instead of parsing the label. check_extraction.py --write-csv fills it from duration_weeks when blank.
